newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds up, yield spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds up, yield spreads widen.

text.p: Prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded near session highs in the late afternoon on Thursday, but yield spreads to Treasuries remained a few ticks wider following a market-friendly retail sales report earlier in the day, traders said.
"Mortgages lagged a bit, and it seems like (spreads) are just starting to come in at this point," said one Ginnie trader in New York.
The widening of mortgage spreads is a function of how mortgage product prices tend to lag Treasuries during a government debt market rally, he explained.
"I expect to see some good buying, especially in 30-year product, if (spreads) stay out this way," the trader added.
At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 15/32 at 100-18/32 bid, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 13/32 at 100-16/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues were up 14/32 at 100-21/32 bid.

Treasury prices enjoyed a strong rally after the Commerce Department said retail sales slipped 0.1 percent in May, contrary to forecasts for a 0.4-percent gain. April's first reported 0.3-percent drop was revised down to 0.9-percent.
The five-year Treasury note was up 16/32 to yield 6.34 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 23/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
Friday, the Labor Department is scheduled to release the U.S. producer price index (PPI) for May at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
The May PPI is expected to rise 0.1 percent in both the overall measure and the core, which excludes volatile food and energy items, based on a Reuter poll.
